div.head: V Atr 9
div.ab: Fulgeorne hy witan, þæt hy nagon mid rihte þurh hæmedþing wifes gemanan.
Fulgeorne hy witan, þæt hy nagon mid rihte þurh hæmedþing wifes gemanan.
Fulgeorne hi wican, þæt hi nagan mid rihte þurh hæmedþingc wifes gemanan.
Fulgeorne hi wi[t]an þæt hi nagan mid rihte þurh hæmedþingc wifes gemanan.
Fulgeorne hy witan þæt hy nagon mid rihte þurh hæmedþing wifes gemanan.
Recht genau wissen sie, dass sie von Rechtswegen keine Gemeinschaft mit einer Frau durch Beischlaf haben dürfen.
They know full well that they may not lawfully have intercourse with a woman.
They know full well that they have no right to marry.
They know full well that they may not rightly have sexual intercourse with a woman.
They know full well that they may not rightfully engage in sexual relations with a woman.

note.seg: = VI Atr 5, 1 = I Cn 6, 2. Den Zusatz VI 5, 2 übernimmt jener Homilet. Fulgeorne witan ist Homilien-Redensart; Hom. n. Wulfstan 157. 161. Vgl. Gl Cölibat
= VI Atr 5, 1 = I Cn 6, 2. The addition VI 5, 2 is taken over by that homilist. Fulgeorne witan is a homiletic turn of phrase; Hom. n. Wulfstan 157. 161. Cf. Gl Cölibat
Cf. I Edm. 1; IV Edg. 1, 7; VI Atr. 5, 1; VIII, 30; I Cn. 6, 2; Wulfstan, p. 269.
A homiletic phrase. The verb may be either indic. or subj. so that it might also be translated, ‘let them know full well.’
